name: ShopSmart breach response
source: DPDP Act 2023 s.2(u), s.8(5)-(6); DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 7; CERT-In Directions of 28 April 2022

detectors.name: Burst of failed sign-ins
detectors.why: Many rejected sign-ins in a short time suggest password guessing or stolen-credential testing. A success after the burst may mean an account was taken over.
steps: Check whether any sign-in succeeded from the same source after the burst
detectors.ref: DPDP Act 2023 · s.8(5) · CERT-In: unauthorised access

detectors.name: Services holding personal data are failing
detectors.why: Loss of access to personal data is a personal data breach under s.2(u) when it compromises availability, e.g. customers cannot reach their account or orders.
steps: Confirm whether personal data was unavailable or lost, or only the service was slow
Restore service and check data integrity
Record the duration and the customers affected

detectors.name: Personal data written to application logs
detectors.why: Card numbers, emails or phone numbers in logs are an accidental disclosure to everyone who can read the logs. The masker caught these; check whether the raw value reached any log store.
steps: Open the log lines and confirm whether it is real personal data or a false match
Purge raw copies from log stores and backups
Fix the code that logged it

detectors.name: Bulk read of personal data
detectors.why: An unusually large number of personal-data rows read in a few minutes is the typical shape of data exfiltration.
steps: Identify the query, caller and destination
Estimate which customers' records were read
detectors.ref: DPDP Act 2023 · s.8(5) · CERT-In: data breach / data leak

detectors.name: Staff opened the full customer list
detectors.why: Viewing every customer at once should be rare and tied to a task. Repeated views can indicate misuse by an insider.
steps: Confirm the staff member had a business reason
Check whether the list was exported or copied

detectors.name: Database errors on personal-data services
detectors.why: Failed writes or lost connections can leave personal data altered, incomplete or unavailable.
steps: Check the SQL state and whether any write was lost
detectors.ref: DPDP Act 2023 · s.2(u) (alteration, loss of access)

detectors.name: Erasure and retention jobs are failing
detectors.why: When the job that erases data fails, personal data is kept after it should have been deleted. Not a breach by itself, but it breaks s.8(7) and s.12(3).
steps: Fix the job and re-run it
Check Retention for customers whose erasure is now overdue
